Let’s break down each term and how they relate:\\n\\n---\\n\\n## 1. `ValidateCreate` in Kubernetes and controller-runtime\\n\\nIn the Kubernetes operator pattern, you often define [webhooks](https://kubernetes.io/docs/reference/access-authn-authz/extensible-admission-controllers/) to validate or mutate resources before they are persisted. In [controller-runtime](https://pkg.go.dev/sigs.k8s.io/controller-runtime) (the de-facto library for writing controllers/operators in Go), you can add custom resource validation using interfaces:\\n\\n```go\\ntype Validator interface {\\n    ValidateCreate() error\\n    ValidateUpdate(old runtime.Object) error\\n    ValidateDelete() error\\n}\\n```\\nWhen you implement `ValidateCreate`, Kubernetes will call this automatically during a `CREATE` operation on your Custom Resource (CR).\\n\\n---\\n\\n## 2. `admission.Warnings`\\n\\nSince **controller-runtime v0.11.0+** (and Kubernetes 1.19+), webhook validation handlers can return warnings to users using the admission API. The new interface looks like:\\n\\n```go\\nfunc (c *MyResource) ValidateCreate() (admission.Warnings, error) {\\n    // ...your validation logic...\\n    // Return some warnings:\\n    return admission.Warnings{\\\"something looks off\\\"}, nil\\n}\\n```\\n\\nInstead of just returning `error`, you can also return a slice of strings as warnings. These warnings are non-fatal; the resource can still be created, but the kubectl/user will see the warnings.\\n\\n- Type: `admission.Warnings` = `[]string`\\n- Docs: [controller-runtime: Returning Warnings](https://pkg.go.dev/sigs.k8s.io/controller-runtime/pkg/webhook/admission#Warnings)\\n\\n---\\n\\n## 3. Example: Using `admission.Warnings` in `ValidateCreate`\\n\\nHere’s a typical pattern:\\n\\n```go\\nfunc (r *MyCustomResource) ValidateCreate() (admission.Warnings, error) {\\n    var warnings admission.Warnings\\n\\n    if r.Spec.SomeField == \\\"\\\" {\\n        warnings = append(warnings, \\\"SomeField is empty, default will be used\\\")\\n    }\\n    if r.Spec.DangerousOption {\\n        warnings = append(warnings, \\\"DangerousOption is enabled, use with caution\\\")\\n    }\\n\\n    if r.Spec.InvalidThing {\\n        // Return error to block creation\\n        return warnings, fmt.Errorf(\\\"InvalidThing cannot be true\\\")\\n    }\\n\\n    return warnings, nil\\n}\\n```\\n\\nWhen a user tries to create this resource via `kubectl`, they’ll see any warnings, but the operation will still succeed unless you return a non-nil error.\\n\\n---\\n\\n## References\\n\\n- [controller-runtime admission.Warnings docs](https://pkg.go.dev/sigs.k8s.io/controller-runtime/pkg/webhook/admission#Warnings)\\n- [Kubernetes Admission Webhooks](https://kubernetes.io/docs/reference/access-authn-authz/extensible-admission-controllers/#admission-webhooks)\\n- [Example implementation in the kubebuilder docs](https://book.kubebuilder.io/reference/markers/webhook.html)\\n\\n---\\n\\n**In summary**:  \\n- Implement `ValidateCreate` for resource admission checks in controller-runtime-based operators/webhooks.  \\n- Use `admission.Warnings` to provide non-blocking feedback during admission.  \\n- Both are recommended modern practices for Kubernetes resource validation.\\n\\nIf you want a full code example or integration step-by-step, let me know!\",\"annotations\":null},\"bing_searches\":null,\"annotations\":null}","detailedContent":"{\"type\":\"output_text\",\"text\":{\"value\":\"It seems you are dealing with Kubernetes **ValidatingAdmissionWebhook** and the Go package **controller-runtime** used for building Kubernetes controllers/operators. The `controller-runtime` library abstracts many Kubernetes API machineries to simplify the implementation of controllers.\\n\\n### What is a DecoderInjector?\\n\\nA **DecoderInjector** is an **interface** that allows you to inject a decoder used for decoding admission review requests in webhooks (such as validating or mutating webhooks) within the controller-runtime framework.\\n\\n**Relevant context:**\\n- It is mainly used in webhook implementations.\\n- The decoder is needed to decode the incoming admission review requests (commonly JSON, representing Its role is to allow handlers to receive an admission `Decoder`, which is used to decode incoming webhook requests into Kubernetes objects.\\n\\nA user typically implements the `DecoderInjector` interface for their webhook handlers so that a `Decoder` can be injected and used to parse the request payloads. However, there was previously an issue for types like `multiValidating` and `multiMutating`, which are unexported types in the codebase, making it impossible for the user to implement this interface for those handlers directly. This problem led to situations where a `nil Decoder` might be injected with certain webhook types in some controller-runtime versions. The typical usage pattern—defining an InjectDecoder method for your handler to receive the *admission.Decoder—remains the same:\\n\\n```go\\nfunc (a *PodAnnotator) InjectDecoder(d *admission.Decoder) error {\\n    a.decoder = d\\n    return nil\\n}\\n```\\nExample of handler:\\n```go\\ntype PodAnnotator struct {\\n    Client  client.Client\\n    decoder *admission.Decoder\\n}\\n\\nfunc (a *PodAnnotator) Handle(ctx context.Context, req admission.Request) admission.Response {\\n    pod := &corev1.Pod{}\\n    err := a.decoder.Decode(req, pod)\\n    if err != nil {\\n        return admission.Errored(http.StatusBadRequest, err)\\n    }\\n    // your logic here\\n    return admission.PatchResponseFromRaw(req.Object.Raw, marshaledPod)\\n}\\n```\\nHowever, in v0.15, some users encountered nil pointer dereferences, likely because InjectDecoder was not called or the decoder was not injected properly. The GitHub issue #2504 documents this, indicating that after upgrading, handlers were getting a nil decoder, leading to runtime panics【3:0†source】.\\n\\nRecommendations:\\n- Double-check the registration of your webhook and handler.\\n- Make sure your handler implements the InjectDecoder interface as expected in controller-runtime.\\n- Ensure that your webhook setup follows the current practices in the version's documentation and examples.\\n\\nIt is likely that changes in lifecycle, webhook registration, or backing DI mechanisms introduced or exposed races or misconfigurations related to injection.\\n\\nLinks:\\n- [Issue discussing InjectDecoder and admission.Decoder in v0.15](https://github.com/kubernetes-sigs/controller-runtime/issues/2504)【3:0†source】.\\n- [Source code of DecoderInto utility](https://github.com/kubernetes-sigs/controller-runtime/blob/v0.15.0/pkg/webhook/admission/decoder.go) that may be relevant【3:1†source】.\\n- Example of InjectDecoder in
